title: "Tidy_Sleep_Data"

```{r import-packages}
#| echo: false
# Load all required libraries for this analysis
# here        → file path management (works on any computer)
# jsonlite    → reading JSON files from WHOOP API
# tidyverse   → data manipulation and visualisation toolkit
# naniar      → missing value analysis and visualisation
# purrr       → list manipulation (used by sanitize function)
library(here)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)
library(naniar)
library(purrr)

# Load custom helper functions written for this project
# Includes: load_data(), sanitize_data_structure(),
#           outlier_detection(), apply_timezone_offset()
source("util/helpers.R")
```

## Load Data

```{r data_load}
# Load raw sleep data from JSON file saved by the WHOOP API
# load_data() is a helper function that handles the file path
# and JSON parsing automatically — see util/helpers.R
sleep_data <- load_data("sleep")
```

## Data Cleaning

### Step 1 — Fix Data Structure

```{r clean_data_structure}
# WHOOP returns some columns as nested lists with empty values []
# sanitize_data_structure() does two things:
# 1. Converts empty lists [] to proper NA values
# 2. Converts text artefacts "character(0)" to NA
# This must run before any other cleaning or analysis
sleep_data <- sanitize_data_structure(sleep_data)
```

### Step 2 — Check Missing Values

```{r missing_values_analysis}
# Generate a summary of missing values per column
# Shows: column name, number of NAs, percentage of NAs
# Sleep data should have no missing values
naniar::miss_var_summary(sleep_data)
```

Sleep data has no missing values — nothing to fix here!

### Step 3 — Remove Naps

```{r remove_naps}
# WHOOP records naps as separate sleep sessions alongside main sleep
# For this analysis we only want main overnight sleep sessions
# We save naps in a separate variable in case needed for future analysis

# Save naps separately — may be useful for future nap analysis
sleep_naps <- sleep_data %>% filter(nap == TRUE)

# Keep only main sleep sessions
sleep_data <- sleep_data %>% filter(nap == FALSE)

cat("Naps removed:        ", nrow(sleep_naps), "\n")
cat("Main sleep sessions: ", nrow(sleep_data), "\n")
```

### Step 4 — Remove Duplicate Sessions

```{r remove_duplicates}
# Each cycle day should have exactly one main sleep session
# If two sessions share the same cycle_id we keep only the first one
# distinct() keeps the first occurrence of each unique cycle_id
# .keep_all = TRUE preserves all other columns
sleep_data <- sleep_data %>%
  distinct(cycle_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

cat("Sleep sessions after deduplication: ", nrow(sleep_data), "\n")
```

### Step 5 — Outlier Detection

```{r outlier_detection}
# Run automated outlier detection on all numeric columns
# Uses the interquartile range (IQR) method via boxplot statistics
# Returns a list of outlier values, confidence intervals and summary stats
result <- outlier_detection(sleep_data)
```

```{r outlier_analysis}
# Investigate potential outliers found above
# Very short sleep sessions (under 3 hours) — possible recording error
# Very long sleep sessions (over 13 hours) — possible recording error
outlier_rows_duration <- sleep_data %>%
  filter(score.stage_summary.total_in_bed_time_milli / 3600000 < 3 |
         score.stage_summary.total_in_bed_time_milli / 3600000 > 13)

# Very low sleep performance (under 20%) — unusual but possible
outlier_rows_performance <- sleep_data %>%
  filter(score.sleep_performance_percentage < 20)

# Print findings
cat("Duration outliers found:    ", nrow(outlier_rows_duration), "\n")
cat("Performance outliers found: ", nrow(outlier_rows_performance), "\n")
```

All outlier values are physiologically plausible — keeping them in the dataset.

```{r cleaning_complete}
# Data cleaning is complete
# Save into a new variable to clearly mark the transition
# from raw cleaning to feature engineering
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data
```

## Feature Engineering

### Step 6 — Convert to Local Time

```{r calc_local_time}
# WHOOP stores all timestamps in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)
# We convert to local Swiss time using the timezone_offset column
# This gives more meaningful times e.g. "went to bed at 22:00"
# rather than "went to bed at 21:00 UTC"
# apply_timezone_offset() is a helper function in util/helpers.R
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    start_local = apply_timezone_offset(start, timezone_offset),
    end_local   = apply_timezone_offset(end,   timezone_offset)
  )
```

### Step 7 — Calculate Sleep Duration

```{r calc_sleep_duration}
# Calculate how long each sleep session lasted in hours
# difftime() calculates the difference between two datetime values
# units = "hours" returns the result in hours
# as.numeric() converts the result to a plain number for calculations
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    sleep_duration = as.numeric(difftime(end_local, start_local,
                                          units = "hours"))
  )
```

### Step 8 — Convert Sleep Stages from Milliseconds to Hours

```{r convert_sleep_stages}
# WHOOP stores all sleep stage durations in milliseconds
# We convert to hours by dividing by 3,600,000
# (1 hour = 60 min x 60 sec x 1000 ms = 3,600,000 ms)
#
# Sleep stages explained:
# Light sleep → easiest stage to wake from
# Deep sleep  → most physically restorative (slow wave sleep)
# REM sleep   → important for memory consolidation and mood
# Awake       → time in bed but not sleeping
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    # total time spent in bed (includes awake time)
    total_in_bed_hours      = score.stage_summary.total_in_bed_time_milli          / 3600000,

    # time spent awake while in bed (restless periods)
    total_awake_hours       = score.stage_summary.total_awake_time_milli           / 3600000,

    # light sleep stage duration
    total_light_sleep_hours = score.stage_summary.total_light_sleep_time_milli     / 3600000,

    # deep (slow wave) sleep stage duration — most restorative
    total_deep_sleep_hours  = score.stage_summary.total_slow_wave_sleep_time_milli / 3600000,

    # REM sleep stage duration
    total_rem_sleep_hours   = score.stage_summary.total_rem_sleep_time_milli       / 3600000,

    # total actual sleep = deep + REM + light combined
    # note: this is NOT the same as total_in_bed_hours!
    # total_in_bed = total_sleep + total_awake
    total_sleep_hours       = total_deep_sleep_hours +
                              total_rem_sleep_hours  +
                              total_light_sleep_hours
  )
```

### Step 9 — Calculate Sleep Deficit

```{r calc_sleep_deficit}
# Sleep deficit measures how much sleep was needed vs how much was gotten
# Negative deficit = slept LESS than needed (most common)
# Positive deficit = slept MORE than needed (less common)
# baseline_milli = WHOOP personalised sleep recommendation in milliseconds
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    # convert baseline recommendation from milliseconds to hours
    baseline_hours = score.sleep_needed.baseline_milli / 3600000,

    # deficit = actual sleep minus recommended sleep
    # negative value means sleep debt is building up
    sleep_deficit  = total_sleep_hours - baseline_hours
  )
```

### Step 10 — Select Relevant Columns

```{r select_only_relevant_columns}
# Keep only the columns that are useful for downstream analysis
# Drop raw millisecond columns — we now have hours versions
# Drop original UTC timestamps — we now have local time versions
sleep_data_cleaned <- sleep_data_cleaned %>%
  select(
    cycle_id,                               # key for joining with other datasets
    start_local,                            # local time when sleep started
    end_local,                              # local time when sleep ended
    sleep_duration,                         # total hours slept
    sleep_deficit,                          # hours under/over recommended sleep
    baseline_hours,                         # WHOOP recommended sleep hours
    total_in_bed_hours,                     # total time in bed
    total_awake_hours,                      # time awake while in bed
    total_light_sleep_hours,                # light sleep stage hours
    total_deep_sleep_hours,                 # deep sleep stage hours
    total_rem_sleep_hours,                  # REM sleep stage hours
    total_sleep_hours,                      # total actual sleep hours
    score.respiratory_rate,                 # average breaths per minute
    score.sleep_performance_percentage,     # actual vs needed sleep %
    score.sleep_consistency_percentage,     # regularity of sleep schedule %
    score.sleep_efficiency_percentage,      # % of bed time actually sleeping
    score.stage_summary.sleep_cycle_count,  # number of complete sleep cycles
    score.stage_summary.disturbance_count   # number of sleep disturbances
  )
```

## Save Cleaned Data

```{r store_clean_data}
# Save cleaned sleep data as RDS format
# RDS is preferred over CSV because:
# → preserves column data types perfectly (dates stay as dates)
# → faster to load in subsequent analyses
# → smaller file size than CSV
# This file is loaded by notebook.Rmd for the master dataset
write_rds(sleep_data_cleaned,
          file = here("data", "cleaned_sleep_data.rds"))

cat("Cleaned sleep data saved successfully!\n")
cat("Rows:    ", nrow(sleep_data_cleaned), "\n")
cat("Columns: ", ncol(sleep_data_cleaned), "\n")
```
